I cannot say enough good things about Dutton Road Veterinary Clinic and the care they gave Gunner throughout his life. Even though he could be a difficult patient, they always treated him with so much patience, compassion, and understanding. Their prices are also very reasonable compared to other vets and they genuinely try to work with you instead of making an already stressful situation more difficult. My ten year old greyhound needed a full mouth extraction due to canine chronic ulcerative stomatitis. I have been taking her to Dutton Road clinic since I adopted her 8 years ago, because of their expertise with greyhounds and their dental needs. Dr. Quinn took the time to present several treatment options and we decided together that the full mouth extraction would be the best option for her to be pain free as she becomes an older lady. Dr. Quinn and the clinic staff (especially Pat and Leighann) were amazing at answering all of my questions along the way. Dr. Quinn and Leighann spent several hours operating, and were able to remove all 25 remaining teeth, and they took excellent care of her during the process and after. It is now 3 days post-surgery and Nila is healing excellently, and is managing quite well eating even with no teeth. I am so grateful for the team at Dutton Road clinic for providing compassionate and professional care, and for their expertise with greyhounds specifically. I have always felt confident with Nila in their care. It must also be said that their prices are much more affordable than most other vets. This extensive surgery easily may have cost $1,000 more or even greater at another vet. Dutton Road clinic really is a blessing for greyhounds and their families.

I didn't want to write this review because I admire this clinic's mission, its affiliation with a national greyhound rescue, its affordability, and the vets' responsiveness to phone calls That said, the front desk staff and Dr. Berman, in particular, are disorganized and miss important symptoms. They ran the wrong fecal test on my dog and I did not realize it until Dr. Berman mentioned it months later. The practice manager ended up refunding me. Dr. Berman is very laissez-faire and failed to properly treat my dog's persistent diarrhea. She recommended that he stay on a bland diet indefinitely, even though he was losing weight (three other vets have since told me that my dog is now nutrient-deficient). Worse still, I called when my dog was short of breath and lethargic following his regular vaccines at a vaccine clinic. When Dr. Berman responded at the end of the day, she seemed perturbed that she had to call me, didn't even ask me to check my dog's heart rate, and told me to give it a few days and he should be fine. He turned out to have a life-threatening pneumonia and I had to rush him to the ICU two days later. Luckily, he survived after a week in the hospital. Worse still, after I complained to the practice, Megan Orr, the assistant director, called me while my dog was in critical condition and proceeded to berate me for following Dr. Berman's advice and not realizing that my dog needed immediate attention??? She exhibited zero empathy and was completely unprofessional. Look at some of the other poor reviews and avoid this place.

I’m heartbroken to say this clinic’s negligence cost the life of my cat and severely compromised my dog’s health. I trusted Dutton Road for years for routine care, but when serious concerns came up, their lack of thoroughness—and compassion—became tragically clear. My dog showed signs of dental pain. Two different vets, including Dr. Raney, glanced at her teeth without doing a full oral exam and said she was fine. I later discovered she had multiple cracked and rotten molars. Another clinic had to extract 11 teeth. Soon after, I brought my cat in for a sick visit. Dr. Raney attempted to pull my 14.5 lb cat out of his carrier by scruffing him, causing him to cry out in distress. She failed to do a proper exam and assumed dental pain, prescribing medication and scheduling a cleaning. The next day, he became drowsy and had trouble breathing. My husband brought him back to the same clinic, where another vet ordered an x-ray—but failed to recognize a severely enlarged heart. Instead of referring him to emergency care, they gave steroids and antibiotics. He died at home two hours later. Three other vets at different clinics reviewed that same x-ray and immediately identified advanced heart failure—something Dutton completely missed. When we spoke to the clinic’s manager afterward, she reviewed the visit video and claimed that Dr. Raney “never scruffed” our cat. But she did try to—and that attempt alone was enough to traumatize him. Worse, while I was trying to connect my husband to the call—barely able to operate the phone through my grief—I heard the manager laughing loudly with someone else in the background. That moment showed me exactly how much they cared.
Please be careful. In my experience, this clinic demonstrated not just poor medical judgment, but a disturbing lack of accountability and compassion. I don’t want anyone else to suffer the kind of loss we’re living with.
